title: fix(enter): show agent description and output modalities on model rows
author: iotserver24
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #14162

- Shows model descriptions directly on desktop and mobile rows.
- Hides the unreliable requests-per-Pollen estimate for agents; existing price details and capability icons remain.
- Keeps agent output labeled as text, since media-tool results are returned as links.

Updated against main and removed the extra output-modality plumbing that could not affect the current catalog.

gist.headline: Model rows speak for themselves
gist.blurb: Model descriptions now show up right in the list, even on a phone. Agent rows also skip a requests-per-Pollen guess that was doing more guessing than helping.
gist.summary: Model rows now show descriptions on desktop and mobile, hide unreliable requests-per-Pollen estimates for agents, and label agent output as text because media-tool results arrive as links.
gist.impact: Users can compare models without opening each row; agent rows retain price details and capability icons while showing output and usage information that matches how agents work.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model catalog displayed on a retro monitor, with short descriptions visible on each row. Polli reads the rows while the Monitor Robot, representing an agent, holds a little link card; a small text label on its row conveys that media-tool results arrive as links rather than direct media output.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel art garden workspace, a retro monitor shows model rows with short descriptions while a friendly CRT-headed robot holds a tiny link card; beside it, the main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings, wearing tiny reading glasses as she studies the list, small-to-medium in the scene and strictly pixel art, never realistic. Lime green (#ecf874) glows prominently around the monitor and code-plants against a warm cream and soft pastel gradient background; cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes.
